items.title: Hospital stocks slip after SC query on steep cancer drug markups
items.description: In a landmark ruling, the Supreme Court of India highlighted troubling markups on cancer drugs enforced by hospitals, urging a probe into reports of patients being directed to specific pharmacies for their medications. Following this announcement, the BSE Hospitals Index faced a steep 5% drop, leading to notable losses for industry giants like Apollo Hospitals and Fortis Healthcare.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Benchmark indices faced a decline as global uncertainty impacted the market and investor sentiment remained cautious. The Nifty index is under pressure, with 22,600 acting as a significant support level. Foreign portfolio investors recorded a net sale of shares worth Rs 10,148 crore while domestic institutions were net buyers. The rupee settled flat against the US dollar amidst heavy FII outflows.

items.title: Stocks in news: Infosys, HDFC Bank, Jio Financial, IRFC, NCC and Blue Dart
items.description: Indian equity benchmarks experienced a decline over two sessions due to profit booking and rising oil prices. The Nifty 50 index closed down by 95.75 points, reaching 22,620.45. Jio Financial Services and Allianz Europe B.V. have invested in their joint venture for business operations. Infosys has expanded its partnership with ABN AMRO for AI-driven transformation initiatives.

items.title: Can October turn the tide for Indian stocks after September rout?
items.description: As investors approach October, the landscape is shaped by high crude oil prices, increasing bond yields, and continued foreign selling. Historically, October has favored positive market returns, yet recent downturns could challenge this pattern. With the earnings season on the horizon, corporate profitability, particularly within large-cap stocks, will be under scrutiny.

items.title: Sebi, RBI join hands to make onboarding easier for FPIs
items.description: In a proactive move, the Securities and Exchange Board of India has teamed up with the Reserve Bank of India to enhance various regulatory procedures. Their primary focus is on making it easier for foreign portfolio investors to enter the market. The launch of the India Market Access portal in September 2025 marked a significant step forward in this initiative.

items.title: Stock Radar: Varun Beverages stock showing signs of rebound after over 20% fall; time to buy?
items.description: Varun Beverages Ltd has shown a strong technical recovery after breaking out of a three-month downtrend channel. The stock regained crucial moving averages, which suggests a potential upward trend for traders.

items.title: Claude, New Yorker, Bandcamp: RBI rules leave international card payments in grey area
items.description: New regulations from the Reserve Bank of India will mandate reporting of international credit card transactions starting October 1. Consumers may need to provide details on all payments for services purchased abroad, leading to potential compliance challenges. The existing framework lacks clarity on how individuals will report these transactions to banks. While international credit card purchases are part of the Liberalised Remittance Scheme, the reporting process remains unclear.

items.title: Rating upgrades moderate in H1 as India Inc faces multiple headwinds
items.description: Rating upgrades moderated in the first half of the financial year as companies faced headwinds from the West Asia conflict, rising crude prices, higher input costs and evolving US tariff measures. Downgrades also declined, though rating agencies cautioned that this may not capture cases where issuers do not cooperate with adverse reviews.

items.title: Highway Infrastructure shares jump 9% after Rs 245 crore toll operations win from UP authority, NHAI
items.description: Highway Infrastructure shares jumped after the company secured toll operations orders worth Rs 254 crore from UPEIDA and NHAI. The key order, worth Rs 220.66 crore, involves toll collection and plaza operations on the Gorakhpur Link Expressway, along with deployment of patrol-cum-safety vehicles.

items.title: $2 billion gone in two days! FIIs accelerate selling as Nifty, Sensex set to fall for 8th week running. Will they make a comeback?
items.description: Foreign institutional investors pulled out over Rs 20,000 crore from Indian equities in two trading sessions as the Nifty and Sensex head for an eighth straight weekly decline. Elevated crude prices, high US bond yields and rate concerns have weighed on sentiment, while analysts differ on the outlook for foreign inflows.

items.title: Stocks to buy: Titan, Lenskart, Dabur among Nomura’s 17 consumer picks. Do you own any?
items.description: With the Q2 earnings season knocking on the door, Nomura expects demand to be largely stable despite the full effect of price hikes. It anticipates increased pressure on margins from higher-priced inventory. It expects volume growth to be largely stable sequentially, while pricing growth will be higher. The international brokerage estimates average EBITDA growth to moderate sequentially for its covered companies to 13.8% YoY, much above its eight-quarter average growth of 7% YoY. Here is a list of 17 consumer stocks on which Nomura has a ‘Buy’ call and its respective target prices.

items.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank shows bullish breakout; check trade setup and derivative strategy
items.description: Kotak Mahindra Bank has delivered a fresh trendline breakout backed by strong volumes and 200-Day EMA support. Trading above key moving averages, technical indicators signal strengthening momentum towards Rs 430. Derivatives analysts suggest a Hedged Call Ratio Spread targeting Rs 420 by October expiry.

items.title: Fortis, Apollo, other hospital stocks slump up to 10% in 2 days after SC questions steep markups. Buying opportunity?
items.description: Hospital stocks extended losses for a second session after the Supreme Court questioned steep markups on cancer drugs and raised concerns over hospitals requiring patients to buy medicines from their own or designated pharmacies.

items.title: Bajaj Auto shares crash 9%, M&M hits 52-week low after September auto sales data. What went wrong?
items.description: Shares of Bajaj Auto and Mahindra & Mahindra (M&M) came under pressure after their September auto sales data, with Bajaj Auto falling nearly 9% and M&M hitting a fresh 52-week low. Bajaj Auto reported a 12% decline in domestic two-wheeler sales, although a 34% jump in exports lifted overall two-wheeler sales by 5% year-on-year to 4.51 lakh units.

items.title: Sensex falls over 100 pts, Nifty below 22,550 as market heads for 8th weekly loss, longest streak in 25 years. More pain ahead?
items.description: Indian equity benchmarks Sensex and Nifty fell for a fourth straight session on Thursday, heading for their eighth consecutive weekly loss. Driven by intense FII outflows and surging US bond yields, the market weakness marks the longest losing streak since 2001, surpassing the seven-week Covid crash.

items.title: AI pressure, client caution cloud Indian IT earnings in September quarter
items.description: India's top IT firms are bracing for underwhelming earnings as they revise annual revenue growth expectations downward. The duel of AI-induced pricing pressures alongside restrained client spending is squeezing profit margins in the industry. Analysts predict a gradual sequential revenue rise ranging from 0.7% to 3.5% for the major players, while even giants like Infosys may lower their projections.

items.title: Jefferies is bearish TCS, Wipro, 6 other IT stocks ahead of Q2 results. How many do you own?
items.description: Jefferies expects revenues across its IT coverage universe to grow 1.7% QoQ in constant currency (cc) during 2QFY27, translating to 4.0% YoY growth, largely driven by acquisitions. On an organic basis, growth is expected to be much slower at 0.8% QoQ and 1.9% YoY. Mid-sized IT companies are expected to grow 3.5% QoQ, while large IT firms may see growth of just 0.5% QoQ, making 2QFY27 the weakest second quarter for large IT companies in the past three years. Here are 9 stocks analysts are bearish on.

items.title: Nifty 500’s hidden bear market: Half the stocks are down over 30% from highs
items.description: In the latest market analysis, it has been observed that about 50% of Nifty 500 stocks have significantly declined from their peak levels. A staggering 252 stocks have seen a drop of over 30%, with 102 stocks plummeting more than 50%. This downturn impacts large-cap stocks broadly. Although there’s a possibility of a relief rally, foreign selling pressures pose continued risks.

items.title: Code red! NSE breadth breaks down as 350 out of 500 stocks crash up to 60% in two month selloff
items.description: In recent weeks, the NSE 500 index has faced significant setbacks, with declines in numerous stocks due to mounting economic pressures and foreign selling activities. Stock losses have ranged between 18% to 64% over the past two months. Contributing factors, such as surging crude oil prices and higher US bond yields, have turned market sentiment sour.

items.title: Cupid shares hit fresh 52-week high as firm raises FY27 revenue, profit guidance again; multibagger stock skyrockets 617% in a year
items.description: Cupid shares hit a 52-week high after raising its FY27 guidance for the second time in two weeks, targeting Rs 800 crore revenue and Rs 250 crore net profit. Driven by strong domestic and international demand, the multibagger stock has surged 617% over the past year.

items.title: Jefferies picks 6 hospitals as Buy after steep correction offers 'excellent' entry points. Check target price
items.description: Jefferies has maintained a Buy rating on six hospital stocks, including Apollo Hospitals and Fortis Healthcare, following a sharp correction driven by regulatory concerns over drug and consumable price caps. The brokerage expects strong fundamentals and strategic price adjustments to help limit long-term EBITDA impact.

items.title: Dr. Lal PathLabs among 3 stocks that closed above VWAP
items.description: On September 30, three stocks in the Nifty 500 pack closed more than 2% above their respective volume-weighted average prices (VWAPs), according to StockEdge’s technical scan data.A closing price above the VWAP indicates that a stock ended the trading session higher than its volume-weighted average traded price for the day. VWAP gives greater weight to prices at which higher trading volumes occurred.

items.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank shares jump 4% to 8-month high after Anup Kumar Saha named CEO. What Nomura, Jefferies expect
items.description: Shares of Kotak Mahindra Bank rose 4% following the announcement of Anup Kumar Saha's appointment as MD and CEO. Saha, currently an Executive Director, has over 32 years of experience in financial services. He will succeed Ashok Vaswani, who decided not to seek reappointment for personal reasons. Brokerages have indicated that Saha's appointment should benefit the bank's strategic direction and stability.

items.title: Max Healthcare Institute among 3 F&O stocks with a sharp rise in futures open interest
items.description: As of September 30, three stocks in the NSE F&O segment recorded a rise of more than 7% in futures open interest compared with the previous trading session, according to StockEdge F&O scan data. A notable increase in futures open interest indicates a substantial rise in the number of active, unexpired futures contracts in a security. This may reflect market participants initiating new positions or increasing the size of their existing positions.

items.title: Sebi revamps Document Number Verification System, adds subject matter as mandatory field
items.description: Sebi has revamped its Document Number Verification System, making a letter’s subject matter mandatory for authentication. The upgraded system aligns with Sebi’s E-Office format and lets recipients verify physical letters, notices and show-cause notices issued by the regulator.

items.title: RBI eases bank stake rules, allows one-time approval for MFs, insurers for holdings up to 10%
items.description: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on Thursday finalised its July proposal to simplify bank shareholding rules, allowing eligible mutual funds, insurance companies and pension funds to seek one-time approval for subsequent acquisitions of major shareholding of up to 10 per cent in the same bank.

items.title: Bharat Dynamics among 5 capital goods stocks that hit 52-week lows and slipped up to 17% in a month
items.description: On Thursday, the benchmark Sensex declined 570 points to close at 71,909. Amid the broader market weakness, five stocks from the BSE Capital Goods Index touched fresh 52-week lows, marking their lowest price levels in the past year. A 52-week low refers to the lowest price at which a stock has traded over the past year and is commonly used as an indicator of its recent price performance.

items.title: Sebi asks stock brokers to display investor warnings on apps and websites
items.description: Sebi orders stock brokers to display investor awareness messages on websites and trading apps under Project Jagrook. From November 1, apps must show Sebi messages and risk disclosures on alternate days, strengthening digital investor education and risk communication.

items.title: Weekly Top Picks: These stocks scored 10 on 10 on Stock Reports Plus
items.description: Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, undertakes detailed company analysis for 4,000+ listed stocks. In addition to detailed company analyses, the report also collates analysts’ forecasts and trend analysis for each component. An average score in Stock Reports Plus is calculated by undertaking quantitative analysis of five key investment tools – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum

items.title: Market wrap: Infosys, HDFC Bank, Bajaj Auto, Maruti Suzuki among top gainers and losers on Nifty and Sensex on Thursday
items.description: Indian equities extended their decline as elevated crude oil prices and multi-year high bond yields intensified concerns over the 2026–27 economic outlook. Nifty fell 0.88% and Sensex 0.79%, while broader markets weakened and India VIX climbed sharply.

items.title: Kotak warns small and midcap euphoria may turn sour as investors chase quick returns
items.description: India’s stock market shows a sharp divide, with investors favouring small and midcaps despite stretched valuations while overlooking relatively attractive largecaps. Kotak Institutional Equities says price momentum and popular growth narratives are driving sentiment more than underlying value and fundamentals.

items.title: 10 microcap stocks slumped up to 32% in just one month. Were they in your portfolio?
items.description: The Nifty Microcap 250 index has remained largely flat but in negative territory over the past month, masking a sharper sell-off across several individual constituents. Within the index, as many as 48 stocks have declined more than 10% during the period. Here, we take a closer look at the 10 Nifty Microcap 250 stocks that have fallen between 15% and 32% over the past month, highlighting the sharp declines in the segment. (Data Source: ACE Equity)

items.title: AMC stocks face rough waters; Kotak sees selective opportunities in SBI, HDFC AMC
items.description: Indian asset management companies are experiencing steady retail inflows, notably through Systematic Investment Plans. Kotak Institutional Equities suggests that future growth is closely tied to market recovery and continuous fund performance. Smaller AMCs are becoming more popular, whereas larger firms are pressured to deliver consistent results. For significant AMCs like SBI Funds Management, stable performance is crucial for sustaining profit growth.

items.title: PB Fintech shares crash 50% from peak, fall below 2021 IPO price. More downside coming?
items.description: PB Fintech shares plunged 50% from their all-time high to drop below the 2021 IPO price of Rs 980. The sharp six-day selloff follows proposed IRDAI regulatory curbs on insurance distribution, prompting brokerages like Bernstein and Jefferies to cut target prices amid earnings pressure concerns.

items.title: US 10-year yield at 24-year high rattles Nifty, rupee and bond markets. Why is India hit hard?
items.description: The US 10-year Treasury yield surged to a 24-year high, triggering a global bond sell-off and pressuring Indian equities, bonds and the rupee. Higher US borrowing costs are raising concerns over FII outflows, currency weakness, imported inflation and RBI policy. Rising crude prices are adding to the pressure on Indian markets.

items.title: Tata Motors PV shares fall over 3% despite 40% Q2 sales growth; Nifty Auto index down over 4%
items.description: Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles shares dipped on Thursday despite a 40% year-on-year rise in Q2 FY27 sales, while the Nifty Auto index declined more than 4%. The company reported strong growth across passenger vehicles and EVs, with quarterly EV sales rising 90%. Investors are now watching festive-season demand and broader auto-sector trends.

items.title: Stock Market Holiday: Are BSE, NSE open or closed for Gandhi Jayanti tomorrow? Check upcoming market holidays
items.description: The Indian stock market will remain closed on October 2 for Mahatma Gandhi Jayanti, with the BSE and NSE shutting trading. MCX and NCDEX will also remain closed. Investors can check the remaining 2026 market holidays, including Dussehra, Diwali-Balipratipada, Guru Nanak Jayanti and Christmas, ahead of the upcoming trading sessions.

items.title: Two tractor stocks: Escorts Kubota shares fall 6%; VST Tillers shares rally 5% after September sales
items.description: Escorts Kubota shares fell sharply on Thursday after September tractor sales declined 16.7% year-on-year, while VST Tillers shares rose 5% as total sales jumped 33%. Escorts cited a high base, festive season shift, patchy monsoon and lower Kharif sowing. Brokerages expect rural demand, festive buying and improving liquidity to support auto-sector volumes.

items.title: 8 weeks, 2,149 points gone: Nifty’s longest losing streak in 25 years raises bear market fears
items.description: The Nifty’s record losing streak has deepened as foreign investor outflows, elevated US bond yields, and geopolitical tensions weigh on sentiment. Analysts say markets remain sensitive to developments in the US-Iran conflict and crude prices, despite resilient domestic growth. Technicals point to a weak near-term outlook.

items.title: MTNL shares rally 17% as board approves Rs 892 crore Powai property sale amid debt worries
items.description: MTNL shares rose sharply after the company’s board approved the sale of its Powai property in Mumbai to the Income Tax Department for Rs 891.53 crore. The asset monetisation comes as the debt-laden PSU seeks to reduce liabilities, which stood at around Rs 40,000 crore in FY26, according to the government.
